mainTopic: Insulating food on שבת (הטמנה): keeping cold food cold, רב נחמן's conduct, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's leniencies
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that allows pulling buried turnips and radishes out on שבת, which refutes רב הונא and שמואל with a תיובתא. A new משנה then teaches three rules. You may not start covering a pot after dark. You may re-cover a pot that was covered before שבת and then got uncovered. You may put a jug of cold water under a pillow. שמואל rules that cold food may be insulated, and אביי explains that this holds even for food people normally insulate hot. A report that רבי forbade it is answered by a story: רבי changed his mind after hearing that רבי יוסי allowed it, and רב פפא praises the respect between them. רבי אמי was upset when רב נחמן insulated cold food and drank water heated by a non-Jewish cook, even though רב נחמן followed שמואל and רב, because an אדם חשוב should be stricter. Finally, a ברייתא gives leniencies of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about טמינה: swapping insulation, insulating after pouring into a second urn, and taking out and returning a pot under coverings that may or may not be moved. The last case, a fully covered pot, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: buried vegetables may be pulled out on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about turnips and radishes buried under a vine finishes. It says there is no problem of כלאים, שביעית, or מעשר, and they may be pulled out on שבת. This challenges רב הונא and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no problem of כלאים, no problem of שביעית, no problem of מעשר, and they may be taken out on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא it began on the previous page. It uses this ברייתא to attack רב הונא and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about someone who buries turnips or radishes under a vine. It says this is not planting, so none of the planting rules apply. The key words are the last ones: the vegetables may be pulled out on שבת. That contradicts רב הונא and שמואל, who worried that pulling them out would move earth on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures. Here it means planting food crops in a vineyard.
The Sabbatical year, when working the land is forbidden
Tithes that must be taken from produce
They may be taken or pulled out

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the end of a ברייתא quoted before This amud begins. Only the last phrase, 'and they may be taken on שבת', is the actual attack.

phrases.english: Not because of diverse kinds (כלאים),
phrases.notes: Burying is not planting, so this is not forbidden planting in a vineyard.

phrases.english: and not because of the Sabbatical year,
phrases.notes: It is not counted as working the land.

phrases.english: and not because of tithes,
phrases.notes: Taking them out is not like harvesting, so there is no new tithe obligation.

phrases.english: and they may be taken out on Shabbat!
phrases.notes: This is the part that contradicts רב הונא and שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues a challenge that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא and שמואל, who worried about moving earth when pulling out buried vegetables on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא plainly permits pulling the vegetables out on שבת. So moving the earth is not a concern.

steps.title: The challenge stands: a full refutation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב הונא and שמואל are refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits there is no answer. רב הונא and שמואל are disproven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תיובתא means the attack fully succeeds. No defense is offered. The ruling that buried vegetables may be pulled out on שבת stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation, meaning the opinion is disproven

steps.whatToRemember: Buried turnips and radishes with some leaves showing may be pulled out on שבת. The worry about moving earth, held by רב הונא and שמואל, is rejected.

phrases.english: A refutation.
phrases.notes: The opinion is knocked down, and the discussion ends here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This closes the challenge from step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא and שמואל are refuted. Pulling out the buried vegetables on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: משנה: covering a pot on שבת, and keeping cold water cold
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה gives three rules. A pot not covered before dark may not be covered on שבת. A pot that was covered and then got uncovered may be covered again. A jug of cold water may be put under a pillow or cushion.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not cover it while it was still day, he may not cover it after dark. If he covered it and it became uncovered, he may cover it again. A person may fill a jug and put it under a pillow or under a cushion.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets rules for covering (insulating) food on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates starting insulation on שבת, which is forbidden, from restoring insulation that was already in place before שבת, which is allowed. It then adds that putting cold water under a pillow is allowed, because that keeps it cold rather than hot.

keyTerms.meaning: While it is still day, meaning before שבת begins
After it gets dark, meaning once שבת has begun

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the base for the rule that you may not start insulating hot food on שבת but may cover it again if it got uncovered. The last line about cold water is the source the גמרא discusses next.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: A new משנה begins.

phrases.english: If he did not cover it while still day —
phrases.notes: This refers to insulating a pot of hot food.

phrases.english: he may not cover it after dark.
phrases.notes: You may not begin insulating on שבת.

phrases.english: If he covered it and it became uncovered,
he is permitted to cover it.
phrases.notes: Covering it again is allowed because it was already insulated before שבת.

phrases.english: He may fill the jug
phrases.notes: This means with cold water.

phrases.english: and put it under the pillow
or under the cushion.
phrases.notes: This keeps the water from warming up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts a new topic after the תיובתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may not start insulating on שבת. You may restore insulation that was in place before שבת. You may insulate cold water to keep it cold.

steps.title: שמואל: you may insulate cold food on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: insulating cold food on שבת is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: It is permitted to insulate something cold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling of שמואל: you may wrap up cold food on שבת to keep it cold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Insulating hot food on שבת is a problem. שמואל says insulating cold food is fine, and we do not worry that it will lead people to insulate hot food. This ruling is the target of the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
To insulate or wrap up food to keep its temperature

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It is permitted to insulate the cold.
phrases.notes: This means keeping cold food cold on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is an אמורא's ruling on the subject of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Insulating cold food on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the משנה already says this
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks what שמואל adds, since the משנה already allows putting a cold jug under a pillow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is he teaching us? We already learned: A person may fill a jug and put it under a pillow or under a cushion!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges שמואל. Why say something the משנה already teaches?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's statement should teach something new. The משנה already allows covering a cold jug with a pillow, which is insulating something cold. So שמואל's ruling looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? This asks what new point a statement adds.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
A person may fill a jug
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 3.

phrases.english: and put it under the pillow
or under the cushion!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges שמואל's ruling as already stated in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that cold food may be insulated
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already permits insulating cold water, so שמואל's statement seems to add nothing.

steps.title: אביי: שמואל includes food that is usually insulated hot
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that שמואל teaches something new. From the משנה alone, we might think only things not usually insulated may be insulated cold. שמואל includes even foods that are usually insulated hot.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: He teaches us a lot. If we had only the משנה, I would have said that applies only to something that people do not usually insulate. But something that people usually insulate, no. So he teaches us that it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends שמואל. He shows that the ruling goes further than the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water is not usually insulated to keep it hot, so allowing it to be insulated cold carries no risk of confusion. With food that people do insulate hot, we might worry someone will slip into insulating it hot on שבת. שמואל teaches that even such food may be insulated when it is cold.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (the initial assumption)
Its usual way, what is normally done with it

steps.whatToRemember: Insulating cold food on שבת is allowed. This holds even for foods people normally insulate to keep hot. This is שמואל's new point beyond the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not repeating the משנה. The משנה's case is water, which nobody insulates hot. שמואל's point is about food that people do insulate hot.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
He teaches us a lot,
for if it were from the Mishna alone,
I would have said these words apply only to —
something that is not usually insulated,
phrases.notes: Like water in the משנה.

phrases.english: but something that is usually insulated, no —
phrases.notes: This means food that people normally insulate to keep hot.

phrases.english: he teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: Even such food may be insulated when it is cold.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּבָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּאִי מִמַּתְנִי׳ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a new point (חידוש) beyond the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the משנה we might think insulating cold is allowed only for things not usually insulated hot.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל teaches that even things usually insulated hot may be insulated when cold.

steps.title: Insulating cold food on שבת is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes a ruling that it is forbidden to insulate cold food on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: It is forbidden to insulate cold food on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new statement that is the opposite of what שמואל said earlier. It says you may not wrap cold food on שבת to keep it cold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, שמואל allowed insulating cold food. This statement takes the strict view. The rest of this section will test it against a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: To insulate or wrap food, to keep its temperature

steps.confusionAlert: Our text reads 'אמר רב', but the next steps are clearly about the view of רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא). The flow of the גמרא reads it as 'אמר רבי'. Read the statement as רבי's ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rav (Rabbi):
phrases.notes: From the way the discussion goes, this is the view of רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: It is forbidden to insulate cold food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a strict view that stands against שמואל's lenient view from Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Insulating cold food on שבת is forbidden.

steps.title: A ברייתא says רבי permitted it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the statement from a ברייתא that says רבי allowed insulating cold food.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: רבי permitted insulating cold food!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question: a ברייתא says the same רבי allowed insulating cold food. So how can he also have forbidden it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same person seems to hold two opposite rulings. The ברייתא says 'permitted' and רב הונא's report says 'forbidden'. The גמרא needs to explain the contradiction.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי הִתִּיר לְהַטְמִין אֶת הַצּוֹנֵן!
phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi permitted insulating cold food!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 7 with a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי forbade insulating cold food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא records רבי himself permitting it, which contradicts the report.

steps.title: רבי changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: Both reports are true: רבי forbade it at first, and allowed it after hearing from רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling (forbidden) was before he heard from רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי. That ruling (permitted) was after he heard from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reports come from two different times. רבי changed his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction is solved by time, not by different cases. The strict ruling was רבי's first view. The lenient ruling is his later and final view, after he heard new information.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This was before he heard it
from Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei;
that was after he heard it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Chronological: an earlier ruling was later taken back.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי held two opposite views at the same time.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי first forbade it and later permitted it. The later ruling is his final view.

steps.title: The story of how רבי changed his ruling
steps.stepSummary: A story shows רבי taking back his strict ruling after hearing that רבי יוסי had allowed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As in this story: רבי sat and said, 'It is forbidden to insulate cold food.' רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said to him, 'My father allowed insulating cold food.' רבי said, 'The Elder has already ruled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that supports its answer. It shows the exact moment רבי changed his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story proves the 'before and after' answer from Step 9. When רבי heard that the older scholar רבי יוסי had allowed it, he accepted that ruling and did not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: As in this case; opens a supporting story
The Elder has already ruled. רבי gives way to רבי יוסי's ruling

phrases.english: As in this case, where Rabbi sat and said:
It is forbidden to insulate cold food.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said before him:
Father permitted insulating cold food.
He said: The Elder has already ruled.
phrases.notes: רבי takes back his strict ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 9 with a story.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי changed from forbidding to permitting.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי's final ruling: it is permitted to insulate cold food on שבת. He accepted רבי יוסי's view.

steps.title: רב פפא praises their mutual respect
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא notes that רבי respected רבי יוסי's ruling, even though רבי יוסי would have been like his student.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Come and see how much they loved each other. If רבי יוסי were alive, he would sit humbly before רבי as a student. We know this because his son רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, who was as great as his father, sat humbly before רבי. And still רבי said, 'The Elder has already ruled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the halacha to learn a lesson from the story. רב פפא praises the love and respect between these scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא reasons from the son to the father. The son was as great as his father and sat before רבי as a student, so רבי יוסי would have done the same. Even so, רבי gave way to רבי יוסי's ruling. That shows great humility and respect.

keyTerms.meaning: Sitting humbly, like a student before his teacher
Fills his fathers' place; as great as his father

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה מְחַבְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.english: Come and see how much they loved one another.
For had Rabbi Yosei been alive,
he would have sat humbly before Rabbi.
For Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei,
who filled his fathers' place,
sat humbly before Rabbi,
and yet he (Rabbi) says: The Elder has already ruled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה מְחַבְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson about character from the story in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not a legal ruling. It is a lesson about the humility and love between great scholars.

steps.title: רב נחמן's instructions and רבי אמי's anger
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells his servant to insulate cold food and to bring water heated by a non-Jewish cook. רבי אמי is upset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to דרו, his servant: Insulate cold food for me, and bring me water that a non-Jewish cook heated. רבי אמי heard and was upset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a practical story. רב נחמן acted leniently in two ways, and רבי אמי did not approve. The story sets up רב יוסף's defense in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two lenient acts are involved: insulating cold food on שבת, and drinking water cooked by a non-Jew (בישולי גויים). רבי אמי's anger raises the question of whether רב נחמן did something wrong.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְדָרוּ עַבְדֵּיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Daru his servant:
Insulate cold food for me,
and bring me water
that a gentile cook heated.
Rabbi Ami heard and was upset.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְדָרוּ עַבְדֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי's ruling to a real-life case of insulating cold food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן acted leniently on insulating cold food and on water heated by a non-Jew. רבי אמי objected.

steps.title: רב יוסף defends רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks why רבי אמי was upset, since רב נחמן followed his own teachers, רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Why was he upset? רב נחמן acted like his teachers. In one matter he followed רב, and in one matter he followed שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רבי אמי's anger. רב נחמן had good sources for both things he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'why was he upset?' is not really asking for information. It pushes back against the anger. Someone who follows his own teachers' rulings has done nothing wrong.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
What is the reason he was upset?
He acted in accordance with his teachers:
one like Rav, and one like Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי אמי's anger in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's anger at רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן followed his own teachers, so there was no reason to be upset.

steps.title: The sources: שמואל on insulating, רב on gentile cooking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the two rulings רב נחמן relied on. שמואל allows insulating cold food. רב says food eaten raw is not subject to בישולי גויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like שמואל: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, 'It is permitted to insulate cold food.' Like רב: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said in the name of רב, 'Anything that can be eaten raw is not subject to בישולי גויים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the exact sources behind רב יוסף's defense. Each of רב נחמן's two actions matches one teacher's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Insulating cold food matches שמואל's ruling from Step 4. Drinking water heated by a non-Jew matches רב's rule: water is normally drunk without cooking, so the ban on בישולי גויים does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The rabbinic ban on food cooked by non-Jews

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's statement here is the same one from Step 4. The גמרא repeats it for a new reason: to show it is רב נחמן's source.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step teaches a basic rule of בישולי גויים: the ban only applies to foods that need cooking. Water and other foods normally eaten raw are not included.
steps.whatToRemember: Each of רב נחמן's actions follows a teacher's ruling. Insulating cold food on שבת is allowed (שמואל, and also רבי's final view). Water heated by a non-Jew is allowed because it is normally drunk without cooking (רב). The next step explains why רבי אמי was still upset.

phrases.aramaic: כִּשְׁמוּאֵל — דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Like Shmuel, as Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
It is permitted to insulate cold food.

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַב — דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Like Rav, as Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא נֶאֱכָל כְּמוֹת שֶׁהוּא חַי —
phrases.english: Anything that is eaten as it is, raw,
is not subject to the ban of food cooked by gentiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּשְׁמוּאֵל — דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sources for רב יוסף's claim in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That רב נחמן's two actions followed his teachers.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling on insulating cold food, and רב's ruling on foods eaten raw and בישולי גויים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both of רב נחמן's actions rest on accepted rulings: שמואל on insulating cold food, and רב on water and בישולי גויים. This sharpens רב יוסף's question, which the next step answers.

steps.title: An important person is held to a higher standard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב יוסף's question. רבי אמי agreed that רב נחמן's actions were allowed, but he held that an important person must be stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי held that an important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why רבי אמי was upset, given that רב נחמן was following his teachers רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not say that רב נחמן did something forbidden. It says that a respected leader should avoid even permitted acts that people might misunderstand and copy in a forbidden way. So רבי אמי's complaint was about רב נחמן's standing, not about the law itself.

keyTerms.meaning: he held / he was of the opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that insulating cold food or using the water heated by the non-Jew is forbidden. The law stays lenient. Only a person of stature is expected to be stricter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the general idea that a leader's conduct is judged more strictly, because others learn from what he does.

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Ami) held
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: an important person is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's question from step 13, after step 14 showed that רב נחמן had sources for his actions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the person: the law is lenient, but a person of stature is held to a stricter standard.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רב נחמן followed רב and שמואל, there was no reason for רבי אמי to be upset.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אמי accepted the law but felt that someone as important as רב נחמן should have been stricter.

steps.title: Adding to or swapping insulation on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that although one may not start insulating on שבת, one may add to insulation that was already in place. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explains how: swap sheets for heavy blankets, or the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Even though they said that one may not insulate food after dark, even in something that does not add heat, if a person wants to add insulation, he may add. How does he do it? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: he takes away the sheets and puts heavy blankets in their place, or he takes away the heavy blankets and puts sheets in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about insulating on שבת. It permits adding to insulation that was already there before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Starting טמינה on שבת is forbidden, even with material that does not add heat. Adding to or replacing insulation that was set up before שבת is treated more leniently. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets a person make it warmer (blankets instead of sheets) or less hot (sheets instead of blankets).

keyTerms.meaning: once it has gotten dark (once שבת has begun)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not allow starting טמינה on שבת. It only allows adding to or swapping insulation that was already placed before שבת.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Even though they said
one may not insulate, even
with something that does not add heat
once it has gotten dark,
if he comes to add, he may add.
phrases.notes: He may add to insulation that was already placed before שבת.

phrases.english: How does he do it?
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He takes away the sheets
and puts the heavy blankets in their place,
phrases.notes: This gives better insulation.

phrases.english: or he takes away the heavy blankets
and puts the sheets in their place.
phrases.notes: This gives lighter insulation, if he is worried the food is getting too hot.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ אֵין טוֹמְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב נחמן story and opens a new ברייתא about the laws of טמינה on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Starting טמינה on שבת is forbidden, but one may add to or swap insulation that was put in place before שבת.

steps.title: Insulating is permitted after pouring into a second urn
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that the ban on insulating applies only to the original urn. If the water was poured into another urn, insulating it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too רבן שמעון בן גמליאל used to say: They only forbade insulating that same urn. But if he poured the water from one urn into another urn, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second leniency from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, about water poured into a new urn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on starting טמינה on שבת applies when the food stays in the pot it was heated in. Once the water is moved to a second urn, insulating the second urn is allowed. The reason is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: an urn or kettle for heating water

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And so too Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel used to say:
They only forbade that same urn,
phrases.notes: This means the urn in which the water was heated.

phrases.english: but if he poured from one urn into another urn, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second leniency from the same תנא in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on insulating on שבת applies only to the original urn. After the water is poured into another urn, insulating it is permitted.

steps.title: The reason: pouring cools the water, so there is no fear of reheating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's logic. Someone who is cooling the water by pouring it will not come to boil it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that he is cooling the water, would he come to boil it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds its own short explanation of why pouring into a second urn makes insulating allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern behind forbidding טמינה is that a person might reheat the food. Pouring water into a cold second urn shows that he is cooling it, not trying to keep it boiling. So there is no fear that he will heat it again.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though this line is phrased as a question, it is not a challenge. It is a rhetorical question that explains the reason for the leniency.

phrases.english: Now he is cooling them (the water),
would he come to boil them?!

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תירוץ (explaining the reason behind the ruling)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the ruling in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pouring into another urn shows that he is cooling the water, so there is no fear that he will reheat it.

steps.title: Removing and returning a pot when the cover is movable
steps.stepSummary: If the top covering is something that may be moved on שבת, he may take the pot out and put it back, even if the material underneath may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he insulated and covered the pot with something that may be moved on שבת, or if he insulated it in something that may not be moved on שבת but covered it with something that may be moved on שבת, he may take the pot out and put it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a rule about taking a pot out of its insulation on שבת and putting it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue here is מוקצה, meaning items that may not be moved on שבת. If the covering on top may be moved, he can lift it and take the pot out. It does not matter if the material the pot sits in may not be moved, since he never has to move that material.

keyTerms.meaning: an item that may be moved on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: There are three leniencies of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טמינה. (1) One may add to or swap insulation that was already in place. (2) Insulating is allowed after pouring into a second urn, because the water has been cooled. (3) One may remove and return a pot when the top covering is something that may be moved on שבת.

phrases.english: If he insulated and covered
with something that may be moved on Shabbat,
or if he insulated in something
that may not be moved on Shabbat
phrases.notes: This is מוקצה material.

phrases.english: and covered it with something that may be moved on Shabbat,
he may take the pot out and put it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with another practical rule about טמינה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the top covering may be moved on שבת, he may take the pot out and put it back, even if the material underneath is מוקצה.

steps.title: When the covering may not be moved but part of the pot is showing
steps.stepSummary: If the top covering is מוקצה, he may still take the pot out and put it back, as long as part of the pot is exposed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he insulated the pot and covered it with something that may not be moved on שבת, or insulated it with something that may be moved and covered it with something that may not be moved, then if part of the pot is exposed, he may take it out and put it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the opposite of Step 19. Here the top covering is something that may not be moved on שבת, and the ruling is: if part of the pot is showing, he may take it out and return it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases are grouped together, and in both the top covering is מוקצה. What lies underneath does not matter. If part of the pot is exposed, he can grab the pot directly and lift it, and the covering just falls off by itself, so he never moves the מוקצה with his hands.

keyTerms.meaning: He insulated (wrapped the pot to keep it hot)
He covered (put a layer on top)
Something that may not be moved on שבת (מוקצה)
Part of it is uncovered, so some of the pot is showing
He takes it out and puts it back

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he is allowed to move the מוקצה covering. He only lifts the pot itself by the exposed part, and the covering slides off by itself.

phrases.english: If he insulated and covered it
phrases.notes: In this first case, both the insulation and the top layer are things that may not be moved on שבת.

phrases.english: with something that may not be moved on Shabbat
or if he insulated it with something that may be moved on Shabbat
phrases.notes: Second case: the bottom layer is fine to move.

phrases.english: and covered it with something that may not be moved on Shabbat
phrases.notes: In both cases the top layer is מוקצה, and the top layer is what decides the law.

phrases.english: if part of the pot was exposed
he may take it out and put it back
phrases.notes: He lifts the pot by the exposed part, and the covering falls off by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָמַן וְכִיסָּה בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיטָּל בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 19. There the top covering could be moved. Here the top covering is מוקצה, and a new condition is added: part of the pot must be exposed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the top covering is מוקצה, he may take the pot out and return it only when part of the pot is exposed, so he lifts the pot directly without handling the מוקצה.

steps.title: Opening the case where the pot is fully covered
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins the opposite case, where no part of the pot is exposed. The ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not (if no part of the pot is exposed)...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The ברייתא starts the opposite case, a pot that is completely covered, and it is preparing to give the ruling, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and if not' flip the condition from Step 20. Now the pot is fully buried under the מוקצה covering, so he cannot grab it without moving the covering himself. This difference is what will lead to a different ruling.

phrases.english: And if not (if the pot was not partly exposed)
phrases.notes: The sentence is unfinished. The ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the reverse of Step 20's condition: the pot is fully covered rather than partly exposed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of a fully covered pot under a מוקצה covering. The ruling follows on the next amud.
